messages:
inc_bot: Incident 2077654321 - Pager triggered: kv-cache mem pressure + NCCL stalls detected across tp group 'tp-24'. Auto-escalation to oncall infra.

maya: seeing huge memory growth on kv-cache shards around 11:03 UTC, paging to NVMe. latency -> 3-6s token tail.

alex: confirmed. continuous-batching rate spiked ~11:02 after a rollout of batch scaler v2. Telemetry shows batch_size target went from 8->64 for long prefixes.

sam: NCCL logs show repeated `rank 3 timed out` and `allreduce failed` from 8-GPU group. likely uneven kv shard sizes causing skew + comm backpressure.

tina (oncall): I'm on it. switching to incident mode. @devops @eng-runtime looped in. who owns batch-scaler config? 

kyle: that was me, pushed a heuristic change to prefer larger batches for short tails. rolled at 10:59. reverting now.

sam: short mitigation proposal:
- flip batch_scaler.enabled=false globally
- roll back batch-scaler v2 in canary and then prod
- force rehash of kv shard placement for tp-24 to even partitions (safe, offline transfer)
- increase NCCL_TIMEOUT and disable NCCL_P2P for the group if stalls continue

maya: customer impact: a subset of production routes (chat-infer-prod) experiencing 20-40% error spikes and high p99 latency. CS reported realtime slowdowns for 3 customers.

customer-success: logged incidents with customers A & B, sending status update: "Investigating, mitigation in progress". asking ETA.

alex: doing global toggle now:
```
# disable continuous batching
curl -X POST "https://internal-api.redwood/services/runtime/config" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"continuous_batching": {"enabled": false}}'
```

deploy-bot: deploy 2077654321-batch-disable started by alex. 3/3 regions success.

maya: CPU tail latency improved immediately on canary. NVMe paging dropped by 70% on affected nodes.

sam: I'm preparing a hotfix for shard rebalancer. plan: compute target sizes then call /kv/reassign with `--drain=true` to move small hot partitions off rank 3.

kyle: I'll sit on the reassign and watch NCCL metrics. pushing fix to canary with a 10m observation window.

tina (oncall): switching primary oncall to alex for incident operations. I'm handing off monitoring and comms.

alex: reassign command (canary):
```
/kv/reassign --group tp-24 --policy even --max-move 4 --observe 600
```

sam: saw one transient retry during reassign, but no NCCL timeouts so far. metrics flattening.

devops: note: nvme ops/sec baseline on node g-14 dropped from 12k -> 2.1k after batch toggle.

customer-success: sent second update to customers with ETA ~30m. they acknowledged.

maya: we should also block the previous batch-scaler change PR until root cause fully identified. PR 4738 reverted.

alex: PR reverted and flagged in release notes. adding an automated canary rule to detect >2x batch growth in 5m windows.

sam: NCCL timeout increase applied to group, and we temporarily disabled P2P which removed a residual stall. still watching for imbalance.

kyle: reassign completed for canary, rolling to prod now with throttled concurrency.

deploy-bot: kv-reassign-progess: 0% -> 100% (rolling 1 node at a time) by kyle.

maya: after full roll, p99 token latency back to normal, error rates trending down to baseline.

alex: closing remediation loop: disabled continuous batching, reverted scaler change, rebalanced kv shards, increased NCCL timeout. preparing post-incident notes and perf regression tests.

tina (oncall): handing back to tina oncall rotation. alex you're primary for the writeup. thanks everyone :thumbsup:

devops: attaching logs and traces: https://telemetry.redwood/incident/2077654321

alex: collecting core dumps + NCCL logs, will attach to postmortem. estimated RCA & postmortem ready by EOD tomorrow.

customer-success: final message to customers: "Services stabilizing; follow-up summary will be provided." :white_check_mark:

inc_bot: Incident 2077654321 resolved by alex at 13:15 UTC. duration ~2h12m. Severity: SEV2. Follow-up required: full postmortem, release-block on batch-scaler heuristic.
